page.overview:
Who is Huitzilopochtli?

Huitzilopochtli was the Aztec sun god and patron god of the city of Tenochtitlan. It is also a god of war and associated with hummingbirds, its name originating from the Nahuatl words for "hummingbird" and either "south" or "left". It's commonly represented as a humanoid figure, sometimes blue-skinned, wearing a feathered hummingbird helmet, and holding the fire serpent Xiuhcoatl. Human sacrifices were performed to Huitzilopochtli, as the Aztecs believed that blood gave it strength and nourishment.

Huitzilopochtli (spelled as "Huitzilopotchli") was mentioned in H. P. Lovecraft's early story "The Transition of Juan Romero" and first incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos in "The Electric Executioner", a collaboration between Lovecraft and Adolphe de Castro. In the works of August Derleth, this entity is associated with Cthulhu.

Juan Romero, while entranced by an inexplicable force or spell, repeatedly cried out this god's name as he descended into a deep chasm inside a mine shaft. On the next day, Romero was found dead in his bunkhouse, with no signs of having left it during the night, and the entrance to the abyss disappeared during a massive cave-in caused by a storm. (: "The Transition of Juan Romero")

The deranged inventor Arthur Feldon believed that Huitzilopochtli and the other Aztec gods were about to return, and that Feldon would rule the world with them with the power of his invention: a portable electric executioner. When another man pretended to be an emissary of Huitzilopochtli in order to play along with Feldon's mania, the inventor was so impressed that he pledged his servitude while mentioning the names of Tonatiuh-Metztli and Cthulhutl. (: "The Electric Executioner")
